title: D3 Claude Code Configuration & Workflows — Attempt D3-A1

questions.prompt: A team adds required project coding standards to one developer’s `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`. A new teammate clones the repository but does not receive those instructions. What is the best correction?
choices: Keep the rules in the user-level file and ask each teammate to copy it manually.
Move the shared standards into the project-level `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
Move the standards into a subfolder `CLAUDE.md` unrelated to the files being edited.
Put the standards into `/memory`, which synchronizes them across the team.
questions.why: The D3 source distinguishes user-level instructions (`~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, only for the individual and not in git) from project-level instructions (`CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md`) intended to be shared.
questions.remedy: Check the scope hierarchy: user instructions are personal; project instructions are version-controlled and shared.

questions.prompt: A team wants a reusable project skill whose verbose generation output should stay out of the main conversation context. Which configuration matches the D3 guide?
choices: Create `.claude/commands/skill.md` and rely on it being loaded continuously.
Create `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and use `context: fork` in its frontmatter.
Create `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` and add `allowed-tools` to it.
Create a path-specific rule with a `paths:` glob; skills cannot isolate context.
questions.why: The D3 source places project skills in `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` and identifies `context: fork` as isolated subagent context that keeps verbose output out of the main session.
questions.remedy: Keep the artifact types distinct: project commands live under `.claude/commands/`; skills have their own directory and SKILL.md frontmatter.

questions.prompt: A repository has test files spread across many directories. You want test conventions to load only when matching test files are edited. Which approach is the best fit?
choices: Add one subfolder `CLAUDE.md` to each directory, regardless of file type.
Use `.claude/rules/*.md` with YAML `paths:` globs such as `**/*.test.tsx`.
Put the test conventions in the user-level `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`.
Create a project slash command; commands load automatically for matching files.
questions.why: The D3 source describes path-specific rules in `.claude/rules/*.md` using YAML `paths:` globs. They load only when editing matching files, which is useful when relevant files are distributed across directories.
questions.remedy: Select path-scoped rules when the target files are spread across folders and matching should be conditional.

questions.prompt: A requested change spans a migration of 45+ files, with several valid architectural approaches. Which workflow best matches the D3 guidance?
choices: Use direct execution immediately because the requested outcome is known.
Use plan mode to evaluate the scope and approach, then execute the agreed plan.
Use direct execution and avoid inspecting the affected files.
Use `/memory` to decide between architectural alternatives.
questions.why: The D3 source recommends plan mode for large or multi-file changes and tasks with several valid approaches or architecture decisions. It also describes combining planning with subsequent execution.
questions.remedy: Use scope and ambiguity as the decision criteria: broad, multi-file, or architectural work favors plan mode; simple, well-scoped fixes favor direct execution.

questions.prompt: Claude repeatedly generates outputs that do not match the team's expected format. Which refinement is specifically recommended in the D3 guide?
choices: Add more vague prose such as “be more careful.”
Provide 2–3 concrete input/output examples that demonstrate the expected pattern.
Move all instructions into a personal user-level file.
Send every unrelated issue in one large message.
questions.why: The D3 source says 2–3 concrete input/output examples beat prose for iterative refinement. It also lists test-driven prompting and an interview pattern as additional techniques.
questions.remedy: Demonstrate the desired transformation with concrete examples instead of relying only on abstract prose.

questions.topic: Non-interactive CI execution and structured results
questions.prompt: A CI job hangs because Claude Code is waiting for interactive input. The team also needs machine-readable findings for inline pull-request comments. Which combination matches the D3 guidance?
choices: Use `CLAUDE_HEADLESS=true` and parse narrative paragraphs.
Run with `-p` / `--print`, and use `--output-format json` with `--json-schema`.
Redirect stdin and rely on Markdown headings as a stable schema.
Use plan mode and ask Claude to print a CSV after the job ends.
questions.why: The D3 source identifies `-p` / `--print` as non-interactive execution and `--output-format json` plus `--json-schema` for structured machine-readable results.
questions.remedy: Separate the two requirements: non-interactive execution prevents CI from hanging; JSON plus a schema makes findings machine-readable.

questions.prompt: A developer fixes issues found by an earlier automated review and pushes new commits. The team wants to avoid repeated comments on already-fixed issues while retaining review quality. What should the pipeline do?
choices: Ask the same session that wrote the code to approve its own changes.
Run an independent review instance, include the prior review results, and report only new or unresolved findings.
Discard all prior results and ask for another broad review without context.
Skip the re-review and rely only on the developer’s commit message.
questions.why: The D3 source recommends an independent instance for review and says re-reviews should include prior review results and report only new or unresolved issues.
questions.remedy: Carry forward prior findings as comparison context, and keep the review independent from the code-writing session.
